[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Path Queries** [CF 1213G · Path Queries](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1213/G){rating="1800"}

Sort the edges by weight and the queries by threshold, both increasing. Raising $q$ only **adds** edges, and in a tree an added edge either joins two different components (merging them) or closes no cycle at all — every edge of a tree bridges. Two vertices are connected at threshold $q$ iff they end up in the same component, so the answer is $\sum_{\text{components}} \binom{\mathit{size}{+}1}{2}$… the sum of "pairs inside each component". When components of sizes $x$ and $y$ merge, new pairs are exactly the $x \cdot y$ cross pairs (pairs already inside either side were counted before) — so one running total, updated by `pairs += x * y` at each union, tracks every threshold in one forward pass. Sizes make the union-by-size trick free here: attach the smaller root under the larger and keep the size at the root. The DSU itself was introduced as a used-early tool (@sec-ds; the Ch. @sec-ds union-find lesson and cses-1091's " Concert Tickets" both lean on it) — this problem needs only `find` and merge-by-size.

[Solved in full in @sec-coord-p2-pathq.]{.card-link}

:::
